title: Rendering, preview and analysis
objective: Keep the one render pipeline and make it smaller, faster and easier to test: a render context per test, one home for limits, a trimmed pixel-domain trait, byte-identical speedups on the tile, frame, resample, threshold, point and proxy paths, a drafted preview that skips work nobody sees, a design for viewport tiles, opaque frames, render.rs split by concept and one test per property, then stage-boundary methods before Corrections adds a new boundary.
context_summary: Rendering has one entry point (luxforge_core::render) with an injected RenderContext, one latest-job worker, one tile function and one point pipeline generic over the byte and linear pixel domains, so a sample equals the rendered byte by construction. The domain unification left a 23-item PixelDomain trait with about ten one-sided items, three separate copies of the resample read-rectangle and two of spatial-entry orchestration in the frame drivers, and a one-megapixel parallel threshold declared five times across two crates. The pipeline also leaves the pool idle during serial tile write-back and frame zeroing, spends three power-function calls per pixel quantizing the byte resample, and runs every pass below one megapixel serially regardless of its actual cost; the core's unit tests, meanwhile, share one static render context again, the same shape of process-global state the render context was built to remove. Every task keeps renders and samples byte-identical and measures its effect before claiming it; the owner's decisions and the programme's constraints are recorded in docs/decisions.md and docs/design/post-consolidation.md.

tasks.description: Give every core unit test that renders its own RenderContext, deleting the shared static test context, its guards and its idle polls.
extra_context: Wave 1, fix. A render context per test removes the mechanism behind a class of load-dependent test failures, before the harness states the rule that depends on it.

`render::testing::context()` (render.rs:1725-1728) is a `static OnceLock<RenderContext>` that every `render::testing` helper (`render`, `render_tiled`, `render_cancellable`, `render_proxy_cancellable`, the linear equivalents, `sample`) renders through, reached directly or through those helpers from 9 files. Tests serialise on `scratch_guard` (23 call sites) and `spatial_guard` (40 call sites), reset the shared estimate store with `clear_estimates()` (51 call sites across 4 files), and poll the shared budget until it drains before asserting exact in-use, peak or estimate counts.

`set_target` and `reset_peak` on `RenderContext` (render/context.rs:125, 205, 223) are `pub` only because tests mutate the shared context's budget target directly, including lowering it to 0 while other tests render through the same context on other threads: the comment beside one such test says exactly that ('other tests' preview workers reserve from it on their own threads').

`RenderContext::new()` is already cheap, and three call sites (preview/tests.rs:582, analysis/jobs.rs:877, resources.rs:244) already build their own context instead of sharing the static one; this task generalises what they already do to every test.

This is the same shape of failure as a recorded flake in the RAW crate's own scratch-permit test: a count that depends on what else the test binary happens to be running concurrently, because both share process-wide state across parallel test threads.

tasks.description: Declare the one-megapixel parallel threshold, the 512 MiB frame limit and the spatial tile size once, in a limits module the core and the RAW crate both import.
extra_context: Wave 2, finish the consolidation. Every speedup later in this group tunes a threshold; each should tune one declaration, not several.

The 1 MP threshold is declared five times: PARALLEL_RENDER_PIXELS (render.rs:36), PARALLEL_PROXY_PIXELS (proxy.rs:27), PARALLEL_CAMERA_PIXELS (source.rs:196), PARALLEL_REDUCE_PIXELS (analysis.rs:34, whose own comment says it mirrors render::PARALLEL_RENDER_PIXELS), and PARALLEL_CORRECTION_PIXELS (luxforge-raw/src/dng.rs:20).

The 512 MiB frame limit is declared four times in three shapes: FRAME_LIMIT_BYTES (proxy.rs:31), MAX_RGBA_BYTES (render/linear.rs:25), a bare 512 * 1024 * 1024 comparison (render.rs:448), and a max_alloc field assignment (source.rs:116). render/spatial.rs's PRODUCTION_TILE is only an alias of SPATIAL_TILE (modules/spatial.rs:16), and render/linear.rs declares its own MAX_SIDE: u32 = 16_384 beside MAX_PIXELS and MAX_SOURCE_BYTES, which the same file already imports from luxforge_raw instead of restating.

luxforge-raw already has a limits module (crates/luxforge-raw/src/limits.rs) that the core imports MAX_PIXELS, MAX_RGB_BYTES, MAX_SIDE and MAX_SOURCE_BYTES from; the shared parallel threshold and frame-limit constants belong there, or in a small module both crates depend on, following that existing pattern rather than a new one.
Every value stays what it is today, only declared once, so renders and samples are unaffected by this task on their own.

tasks.description: Trim the pixel-domain pipeline to one resample read-rectangle rule, one spatial-entry helper and one alpha blend, delete the GRID policy knob, and move the domain-independent no-op checks into Render.
extra_context: Wave 2, finish the consolidation. The generic pipeline is the right design; it should describe only what the two domains actually do differently.

PixelDomain (render/pipeline.rs) has 23 items: 3 associated types, 1 const and 19 methods. About ten are no-ops, identities or unreachable on one side: Byte::frame_pixel (render.rs:1279) is never called because Byte's GRID is SpatialMode::Point (render.rs:1145) while Linear's is SpatialMode::Frames (render/linear.rs:640), so a grid is materialised for one domain and tiled for the other.

The rectangle a resample reads is computed three separate ways: rows_read_by (render.rs:697), tap_region (render/window.rs:113) and a second tap_region (render/linear.rs:977). Spatial-entry orchestration (resolve or reuse handed globals, reduce, call spatial_output) is written out twice, inline in the byte driver and again in render/pipeline.rs; the resample's alpha blend is likewise written twice.

The 8x8 capability sample grid (capabilities/data.rs, SampleGrid8) reads 64 points through Render::grid; because GRID is Frames for the linear domain, a RAW asset with a spatial layer materialises a full spatial frame to answer it, where the byte domain answers the same 64 points by reading tiles.

The two rendering-unification commits added roughly 250 net production lines rather than removing them; this is where that count comes back down. Constraint: renders and samples stay byte-identical on both domains, since the read rectangles being unified are supersets of what each domain reads today, and a windowed downscale already proves equal to the whole one inside it.

tasks.description: Write each spatial tile's batch back with per-row copy_from_slice, produced in the frame's final layout during the parallel phase, instead of copying one pixel at a time on the calling thread.
extra_context: Wave 3, speed. The clearest byte-identical win in the group: the same values move to the same places, only as whole rows instead of one pixel at a time.

run_batches (render/spatial.rs:606-641) evaluates a batch in parallel and then writes it back serially: `for (tile, result) in batch.iter().zip(results) { write(*tile, result)?; }`. Byte::write_tile (render.rs:1261) copies three bytes and calls an alpha closure per pixel; Linear::write_tile (render/linear.rs:815) does the planar equivalent. The pool sits idle during every one of these writes.

Recorded CPU utilisation on the generated fixtures matches a serial write of this size: Clarity at 60 MP renders in 620 ms at 1105% CPU (about 140 ms serial-equivalent), Dehaze in 355 ms at 713% (about 190 ms), Texture in 629 ms at 858% (about 260 ms); the 24 MP figures (193 ms at 1090%, 128 ms at 771%) scale down consistently (docs/specs/performance.md, Presence exact renders on the generated JPEGs).

Proposal: have tile_output (already computed in the parallel phase) produce the tile in the frame's final row layout, then have write_tile copy whole rows with copy_from_slice, one memcpy per row for the byte frame's RGBA rows and three for the linear frame's planes, instead of a per-pixel loop; reuse one scratch buffer per worker in run_tile rather than reallocating and zero-filling it per tile.

tasks.description: Allocate frames as Arc<Vec<u8>> from vec![0; n] instead of a serial byte-by-byte fill, and copy an identity segment's source rows inside the parallel pass instead of up front on one thread.
extra_context: Wave 3, speed. Pairs with the tile write-back speedup: both remove a serial full-frame pass that the parallel pass then overwrites anyway.

zeroed_frame (render.rs:470) is `std::iter::repeat_n(0, len).collect::<Arc<[u8]>>()`, which writes every byte serially on the calling thread: 96 MB at 24 MP, 240 MB at 60 MP, 159 MB for the X100VI's RAW output. Its callers include the resample, a non-identity segment, the byte spatial frame, the RAW linear output, the proxy and JPEG decode. An identity segment with a colour run additionally copies the whole source up front with `Arc::<[u8]>::from(source.rgba.as_ref())` before the parallel colour pass runs.

Proposal: hold frames as Arc<Vec<u8>> allocated with vec![0; len] (fresh pages are already zero and are faulted in by whichever worker first writes them), as LinearImage already holds its planes in Arc<Vec<f32>>. For the identity-with-colour case, let the row loader copy source rows inside the parallel pass, with a row copy_from_slice fast path when the geometry is the identity, instead of copying the whole source first.

This changes the field type of two pub fields on Raster and SourceImage; the desktop and presenter (Frame::new, luxforge-ui/src/photo_surface.rs:157) accept anything implementing AsRef<[u8]>, so a thin wrapper keeps them unchanged. Current shapes only: this is an internal type change, not a catalog or API one.

tasks.description: Quantize the byte resample's bilinear sample through the guarded threshold lookup the RAW terminal already uses, and remove per-pixel LazyLock dereferences and view-layout recomputation from the hot colour and RAW read loops.
extra_context: Wave 3, speed. A straightened crop's resample is the largest per-pixel cost left on the gesture path it serves.

bilinear (render.rs:383) quantizes each of a pixel's three channels with linear_to_srgb (colour.rs:155), which calls the sRGB encode power function once per channel: three powf calls per output pixel. quantize_channel (colour.rs:134), used elsewhere, already answers the same question through a guarded lookup (CODE_INDEX/CODE_THRESHOLDS) with no power function per pixel, and the RAW terminal path already relies on that same guard argument. A 24 MP 10-degree crop outputs about 7.7 MP, so this is roughly 23 million powf calls; instant-preview.md records the straightened crop adding about 30 ms to a 24 MP exact render and about 23 ms to the proxy frame.

Smaller costs in the same loops: decode_pixel and quantize_channel dereference a LazyLock table on every call, an atomic load the compiler cannot merge, up to six times per pixel across the byte colour path. LinearImage::pixel (render/linear.rs:328) recomputes output_dimensions(), view.map() and a plane-length try_from on every call, which any cropped or turned RAW source read pays per pixel; pixel_f64 then re-checks finiteness that construction already proved. The finiteness scan after each colour unit (render.rs:311) short-circuits with all(...), which cannot vectorise.

Constraint: byte identity for the resample change rests on the same guard the RAW terminal already ships with, not on construction alone; extend the existing boundary tests to linear_to_srgb and prove it with full-frame hashes of rotated-crop renders, not only the boundary cases.

tasks.description: Choose each rendering pass's parallel threshold from its measured work per pixel instead of the one one-megapixel constant, so small proxies of heavy stacks still use the pool.
extra_context: Wave 3, speed. PARALLEL_RENDER_PIXELS becomes several thresholds in the limits module this group already gave the constant a home in.

Rule 9 (docs/engineering/performance-rules.md) measured the one-megapixel threshold for the transform pass only: 'The transform pass goes parallel above one megapixel and stays serial below it', a copy costing about 1-2 ns per pixel. The same constant also gates the colour pass (about 77 ns per pixel for a full Basic layer, from the proxy render figures) and every spatial pass (100+ ns per pixel): the colour row pass (render/pipeline.rs), the resample (render.rs) and the spatial stage's own gate (render/spatial.rs, `large`), which decides both tiled parallelism and per-tile pooled passes.

A display-bounded proxy is commonly under 1 MP: a 1080p landscape photo at scale 1 is about 0.96 MP, a portrait or a half-screen window smaller still. A full Basic layer there is estimated at about 74 ms serial against about 5 ms on the pool, and a Presence layer at about 150 ms against about 12 ms. Every drag in a small window falls off this cliff; a large window does not.

Proposal: a threshold per pass kind, declared in the limits module and measured rather than assumed, for example copy-only passes staying at one megapixel, the colour pass going parallel above roughly 64k pixels when the segment has colour, the spatial stage parallel whenever it has more than one tile with pooled per-tile passes when a single tile is large, and the resample parallel above roughly 256k output pixels.

tasks.description: Read tile rows instead of one pixel at a time for point queries through a spatial segment and for the global-estimate reduction that feeds units such as Dehaze.
extra_context: Wave 3, speed. The row reader this task uses already exists and already proves equal to the per-pixel path; this closes the two pulls the domain unification left per-pixel.

PointTiles::pixel (render/spatial.rs:784) fills a tile's input region one pixel at a time through the pipeline's spatial_read -> pixel_in. The global-estimate reduction (render/pipeline.rs and render/spatial.rs's build_reduction / build_reduction_by_tiles) reads every pixel of the stage the same way, and the byte domain's colour_row falls back to PixelDomain's per-pixel default rather than a row implementation. Evaluation::fill_rows (render/pipeline.rs:450) and the row-equals-point contract it already proves are used only by linear frame renders today.

On RAW, the Dehaze global estimate is keyed by the recipe prefix and the exposure bits, so it is rebuilt on every upstream edit and, during a Basic drag, on every input frame. Estimated from the per-pixel cost (not yet a recorded RAW-with-Dehaze drag measurement): the X100VI's 40 MP exact-phase reduction is on the order of 4-5 s of CPU, about 0.3-0.4 s wall, and a 1.65 MP RAW proxy on the order of 190 ms of CPU, about 14 ms wall, per drag frame. The byte path does not pay this, because it reads its already-materialized frame instead.

Proposal: give PointTiles::pixel and the reduction builders a region fetch backed by Evaluation::fill_rows, implement Byte::colour_row with the row arithmetic ByteRows::run already uses, and delete the per-pixel read closures; block_mean keeps summing in the same order so estimates stay identical.

tasks.description: Build the proxy's box downscale in row bands instead of one full-window float intermediate, compile the proxy stage once per job instead of twice, and drop the previous cached proxy before building its replacement.
extra_context: Wave 3, speed. Three independent proxy-build costs the design already bounds in principle but the code does not yet honour.

BoxDownscale::new (proxy.rs:464) allocates one intermediate of window width x every source row the window reads x 3 f32 before its vertical pass runs: 124 MiB for a 24 MP JPEG proxy, 159 MiB for the X100VI, 198 MiB at 60 MP, all at the owner's 2880x1800 display bound. instant-preview.md says the proxy adds at most one bounded buffer; this one scales with the source instead.

proxy_window (render/entry.rs:303) compiles the proxy stage and computes WindowPlan::of, and render_proxy (render/entry.rs:341) compiles and plans again and re-runs the same source checks; a job with a proxy phase compiles its stack more than once per stage. The existing test named for that claim, a_preview_job_compiles_its_stack_once_per_stage_it_renders_at (preview/tests.rs:569), counts only calls to render(), so it does not see the window-plan compile inside proxy_window.
The previous cached proxy (preview/worker.rs, proxy.rs's cache insert) stays alive for the whole build of its replacement, on top of the new intermediate.

Proposal: stream the vertical pass in row bands (about 1 MiB per worker instead of the whole window), each band reading only the source rows it needs with one row of overlap between bands; let proxy_window hand its compiled stage and WindowPlan back for render_proxy to reuse; clear the cache entry before building the replacement.

tasks.description: Measure whether withholding a drafted job's exact phase at Fit while the gesture is moving closes the paint and drag latency tail, and adopt a deferral flag if it does.
extra_context: Wave 3, speed. This measurement is ordered before the masking group's own paint-latency work, so that work can attribute its figures correctly.

Every preview job renders its full-resolution exact phase, and a drafted job also asks for .analyse() (crates/luxforge-app/src/app/tasks.rs, draft_set_now), after its proxy frame (crates/luxforge-core/src/preview/worker.rs). Under a paced stroke or drag that phase is always superseded before it is used, and the next position's job does not start until the superseded one notices, at its next chunk boundary. Recorded preview request-to-worker-start is 6.6/18.2 ms (p50/p95, docs/specs/performance.md, 'Bare recipe at photo size').

The release's commit refresh already renders the exact frame and histogram once the gesture stops, so withholding the drafted exact phase at Fit loses nothing a released frame does not already provide.

Proposal: run editor-latency --mode paint and --mode drag with the drafted job's exact phase withheld at Fit and compare against current behaviour. If it closes the tail, add a job flag that defers a drafted job's exact phase, and its histogram, at Fit until the gesture is idle, tested at the preview queue; update the performance rules' known-costs table with the result either way.

tasks.description: Design viewport-tile rendering for a 100% drag from the window-rectangle walk that already exists, correct the documented blocker, and bring the histogram-during-drag question to the owner.
extra_context: Wave 3, speed. This is a design task: it produces a design section and an owner answer, not the viewport-tile implementation itself.

docs/engineering/performance-rules.md's known-costs table and docs/design/instant-preview.md both say viewport tiles need 'the inverse of the geometry tail over a rectangle, which the crop contract does not define yet'. WindowPlan::of / apply (render/window.rs) already walk a needed rectangle back through exact geometry, a resample and a spatial boundary to a source rectangle, for the proxy window; that is exactly the missing piece, already built and tested.
A 100% drag today renders the whole exact frame per input: about 200-300 ms at 60 MP with a full Basic layer, against about 25 ms for a 2880x1800 viewport (5.2 MP).

Remaining design work: WindowPlan::of_rect starting from the viewport instead of the whole output; a coordinate origin for a finish unit in a cut segment (masks already map through the suffix; a finish unit is handed frame coordinates today); a source-rectangle view (free for RAW's LinearImage::with_view, a parallel copy or an origin offset for the byte path); and the owner's answer on what the histogram and clipping overlay show mid-drag, recommended as keeping them marked updating during the drag, as they already are between a proxy frame and its exact phase, since the full exact frame still renders on release.

tasks.description: Decide whether a spatial operation with a large summed halo runs in larger tiles, so Texture and Dehaze stop recomputing the margin Clarity needs around every tile.
extra_context: Wave 3, speed. Blocked on the owner's decision; measured, not implemented.

A render the spatial target holds to fewer tiles than the pool has workers already spreads each tile's passes over the pool, so a 60 MP render with all three Presence fields uses about twelve cores and takes about 3.4 s. What remains is work repeated in the halo: in 512 px tiles Dehaze computes 5.2 times the stage and Texture 4.9 times, because each tile carries Clarity's 327 px halo, and the render spends about twice the CPU time it did when two tiles ran with serial passes.

Measured with 1024 px tiles and pooled passes on the generated 60 MP JPEG (5 samples, load 8 to 12): all three fields 2.09 s against 3.67 s in 512 px tiles on the same run, Texture and Clarity 1.62 s against 2.63 s, with total CPU time back to the serial-pass figure. One tile's working set is then 208.5 MiB, so batches hold one tile inside the 256 MiB target. The frame was byte-identical to the 512 px render for Texture with Clarity and for all three fields on the 24 MP and 60 MP fixtures.

Samples through a spatial layer are now answered by a dedicated point worker, off the catalog owner, so a larger tile costs only the sampling client its own wait, not every other client: the pointer readout goes from 104 to 107 ms to 217 to 218 ms with all three fields at 60 MP, and from 13 to 50 ms with Texture alone (9 interior points, each equal to the rendered byte), but no longer delays another client's request the way it would when sampling ran on the owner. Byte identity across tile sizes is asserted by tests and holds on these fixtures, but the box passes' running sums start at each rectangle's edge, so it rests on evidence rather than construction.
A tile size chosen from the summed halo (512 px for a small one, 1024 px once it passes some bound) would keep samples through a small-halo stack as cheap as today.

tasks.description: Declare every frame opaque RGBA and delete alpha blending, fetching and threading from the render paths.
extra_context: Wave 4, structure. Follows the frame-allocation change so the byte tile write can become a plain row copy with no per-pixel alpha read.

Owner decision: frames are opaque by contract. Every production byte frame already is: JPEG decode (source.rs) and the proxy (proxy.rs) both write 255, and analysis.rs already documents that the supported JPEG path is opaque.

Despite that, the renderer still blends alpha through resamples (bilinear's alpha average), walks the geometry to fetch a spatial output's input alpha (alpha_in, render/pipeline.rs), and threads an alpha closure through spatial_output and write_tile. It is also inconsistent: the exact path preserves a source's alpha while the proxy discards it, so 'proxy equals the exact recipe over the exact downscale' would not hold for a hypothetical non-opaque source, harmless only because none exists.

tasks.description: Split render.rs by concept into separate files with no logic change, and fold in shared region and segment constructors, one Cancel module, LinearImage beside SourceImage, and the small clean-ups listed below.
extra_context: Wave 4, structure. Landed last among the render changes so the split starts from the final shape, not one later tasks would immediately move again.

render.rs is 5,582 lines, 1,686 of them production, mixing about eleven concepts: Cancel, colour runs, the bilinear resample, Raster and frame helpers, exact geometry and the resample mapping, the compiled IR (Entry / Segment / Compiled), the public locate and transform types, the Byte domain, ByteRows, LayerInput / grid_centres / stage_transform, and the byte driver. Cancel is the crate's general cancellation token, used by latest, analysis and the capability jobs, not only by rendering.
render/linear.rs holds LinearImage, the RAW source's own data type, while the JPEG source type SourceImage lives in source.rs; the two peer types are asymmetrically placed.

Small clean-ups to fold in: grid_centres (render.rs) duplicates cell_pixel (analysis/overlay.rs) without its edge clamp; add Region::EMPTY, Region::whole(stage) and Segment::stage() to replace the ad hoc region and stage literals scattered through render/, mask_field.rs and proxy.rs; the LayerInput enum plus the MaskInputPixel trait (analysis/mask_overlay.rs) have one production implementer and can become one generic impl; analysis.rs's reduction has five entry points (reduce, reduce_cancellable, reduce_raster, reduce_raster_cancellable, reduce_with_threshold) where reduce_cancellable has no caller outside the file; source validation and check_resamples each run twice across render/entry.rs and render/pipeline.rs; LinearRows::load zero-fills its row buffer on every chunk although load overwrites every element; and docs/design/architecture.md's 'Rendering and limits' section says a pool worker allocates its scratch once and reuses it, where try_for_each_init actually calls init once per Rayon split, typically tens of times per pass.
No behaviour change: this is a mechanical split plus the listed deduplication, proven by an unchanged test suite and byte-identical renders.

tasks.description: Prove each rendering property once: one render-equals-sample table over every stack shape and both pixel domains, preview tests that stop re-proving the latest-job worker, injectable thresholds instead of multi-megapixel unit-test frames, and no stale diagnostics.

preview/tests.rs restates latest.rs's superseded, abandoned and delivery-floor behaviour through the preview facade in about 185 lines; only its phase and token tests are preview-specific.

Unit tests reach for 1-10 MP frames only because the parallel and tile thresholds cannot be injected per test; RenderOptions::with_tile already shows the pattern for the tile size. tests/cancellation.rs renders two 24 MP frames whose only point, a 25 ms timing bound, is compiled out `if cfg!(debug_assertions)`, so cargo test pays for 48 MP of rendering and checks nothing timed in the dev profile.

tasks.description: Give the compiled Entry a small set of methods for what its match arms ask today, so a new stage-boundary kind becomes one implementation instead of a new arm in about 30 places.
extra_context: Wave 6, roadmap groundwork. Blocked: starts with the Corrections repair stage, the third kind of stage boundary; a trait is premature with only two kinds in the code today.

Entry (render.rs) is matched across at least 7 files (render.rs, render/pipeline.rs, render/linear.rs, render/window.rs, render/entry.rs, render/spatial.rs, modules/registry/compile.rs) in about 30 places. The Corrections proposal's repair stage would add a case to each: the point walk, alpha_in, the byte driver, Evaluation::new, window planning, locate, transform and the linear rows.

A GPU colour stage would need a per-unit typed description; PointwiseColor (modules/processing.rs) exposes only apply_row and describe, with no way to extract a unit's kind and coefficients. spatial::prefix_hash (render/spatial.rs) already gives an out-of-process AI patch the input-prefix hash its design needs, so that part does not wait on this.

Proposal, once the Corrections repair stage starts: give Entry methods for what the match arms currently ask by hand, an input-stage query, mapping a point back through the entry, the rectangle it reads, materialising it, and evaluating one point through it, so a new stage-boundary kind implements those methods once instead of adding an arm at each of the roughly 30 sites.
